MAGDA Service Desk

This document describes an implementation model, in this case MAGDA-Person Implementation Model. This implementation model answers the question of how the corresponding domain model can be applied in practice. It explains the constraints (cardinality, code lists) and lists the corresponding (RDF) terms.

Summary

The MAGDA-Person Implementation Model is based on the OSLO Person Application Profile to encompass MAGDA's personal services according to this OSLO data standard.

The personal services allow the recipient to retrieve the current data of a person, based on that person's INSZ number. Once the recipient has submitted the request, the request is forwarded to the National Register or the Crossroads Bank of Social Security (KSZ). This depends on the recipient's authorizations and the source choice in the request.

Status of this document

This implementation model has the status Ontwerp Standaard and was published on 2027-01-01.

License

This specification by Digitaal Vlaanderen is published under the "Model License Free Reuse - v1.0".

Conformance

The conformance for implementation models can be found here.

Belgian address

Description
Information that allows for a structured and unique reference to a building unit, a mooring place, a pitch, or a plot based on a municipality name, a street name, a house number, and possibly a bus number and a postal code.
Usage
The definition refers to Belgian addresses. In other countries, an address may refer to other geographical objects (not building units or plots) or consist of other designations (different from house number and bus number) or of components other than street name, municipality name, or postal code. Alternative address indications other than house number or bus number (for example: entrance indication, stair indication, floor indication...) or a building name or room name, etc., are possible through association with address expansion. Exchange of foreign addresses must be done using the object Address Representation.
Properties
No properties are defined for this entity.

Nationality

Description
The relationship between a Person and a state, culture, or loyalty.
Usage
A broader concept than citizenship is limited to the relationship with a state and associated rights and obligations. Anyone who holds the nationality of a particular country is usually automatically a citizen of it. It is usually acquired automatically by birth: one either receives the nationality of one's parents or one obtains it of the country of which one is a resident. But one can also acquire nationality through naturalization. In principle, one then loses their original nationality, but that is not always the case (multiple nationality).
Subclass of
Version
Properties
The following properties are defined for this entity: acquisition , end date , nationality , start date .
Property Expected Type Cardinality Description Usage Codelist
acquisition Acquisition of nationality 0..1 How and where the Nationality was acquired.
end date Date 0..1 Until the time when the instance of this class applied in the field.
nationality STATBEL Nationality Code 0..1 The nationality of the Person.
start date Date 1 From the moment the instance of this class applied to the field.

Person

Description
Natural person.
Usage
In case law, it concerns a person (in the legal sense, that is, with their own legal personality) of the human species, that is, a physical person. The counterpart is the legal person, a legal construct that gives a private or public organization the same legal personality as a natural person (for example, it can also have debts, conclude contracts, be sued, etc.).
Subclass of
agent

Title Title 0..* Reference to the Title of a Person.
usedFirst name String 0..1 The main first name of the person's first names.

Problem details

Description
More detailed description of the error in an HTTP response.
Usage
This is to supplement an HTTP status code, for example with a 400 (Bad request) status code to indicate why the request was bad. Based on RFC7807.
Properties
The following properties are defined for this entity: detail , instance , status , title , type .
Property Expected Type Cardinality Description Usage Codelist
detail String 1 Human-readable description of the error.
instance URI 0..1 Reference to the instance of the object to which the error relates. For example: the reference to the request.
status Integer 0..1 HTTP error code. As described in RFC7231. For example: 404 for "Not Found".
title String 1 Short, human-readable description of the error.
type URI 1 Nature of the error.

date Date 0..1 Date of entry in the Register.
type Register type 0..1 Nature of the Register.

RegisteredPerson

Description
Person whose data are registered in a register.
Usage
Usually, this register is a population register, but it can also be, for example, an electoral register. The registered data relate to the person's identity (for example: first and last name) and place of residence, as well as important life events such as birth, marriage, death, etc. This data is typically registered by the government, provides the registered person, and allows the government to compile basic statistics about its population.
Subclass of
Person
Properties
The following properties are defined for this entity: administrator , registration , registration detail .
Property Expected Type Cardinality Description Usage Codelist
administrator Administrative Manager 0..* Referral to the Administrative Administrator of the person's file. Normally, there is only one administrator present at a person's place, but in exceptional cases, there can be multiple administrators. For example: the person has an address abroad, is moving between municipalities, etc.
registration identifier 1 Identification code of the person in the register.
registration detail Registration status 0..* Reference to detail regarding the Registration of the Person.

Registration status

Description
Status of the Person in the register.
Usage
Provides details about the registration itself, for example whether the registration is still valid and possibly followed by a new registration. The latter is done in the National Register, for example, in cases of errors or changes to the identifier (for example, in case of gender change) that require the registration to be redone.
Subclass of
Version
Properties
The following properties are defined for this entity: canceledFile , end date , file status , reference file , register , start date .
Property Expected Type Cardinality Description Usage Codelist
canceledFile identifier 0..* The previous registration of a Person in the register. Only applicable if a new Registration exists.
end date Date 0..1 Until the time when the instance of this class applied in the field.
file status file status 0..* Status of the Registration file. In the National Register, used when the registration in the register is no longer valid, for example: because the person has been removed from the register, a previous registration was canceled, or the person has died, etc. Link
reference file identifier 0..1 The new registration of a Person in the register. Only applicable if a Registration already exists.
register Register type 0..1 Register in which the Registration takes place.
start date Date 1 From the moment the instance of this class applied to the field.

Residency status

Description
Indicates the state of the Population.
Usage
Typically as a result of research into the conditions of Residency, such as the reality of and the right to residence.
Properties
The following properties are defined for this entity: decision , type , validity .
Property Expected Type Cardinality Description Usage Codelist
decision Document 0..1 Decision applicable to the status of the Residents' Association. In practice, a reference to the document that establishes the Administrative or Legal Decision.
type Residency status type 0..1 The status of the population. For example, a decision made by a government, a housing inspection in progress, etc.
validity Period 0..1 Perdiode to which the status applies. For example, in the case of an entry ban, the period for which it applies.

Datatypes

Address representation

Description
More readable representation with only the basic data of the address, intended for using an address as an attribute of another object.
Usage
For example, as an attribute of a person or building, ... The Address Representation does not only relate to Belgian addresses; it can be used to display foreign addresses (where other address designations than house number or bus number may be used, or where address components such as address areas occur).
Subclass of
Location
Properties
The following properties are defined for this datatype: address area , Administrative Unit Level 1 , Administrative Unit Level 2 , bus number , country , fullAddress , house number , location indication , location name , municipality name , P.O. Box , post name , postal code , refers to , street name .
Property Expected Type Cardinality Description Usage Codelist
address area LangString 0..1 Name of a geographic area or place that groups a number of addressable objects to address them without the area or place being an administrative unit. For example: the name of the hamlet where the address is located.
Administrative Unit Level 1 LangString 0..1 Highest administrative unit of the address, usually a country.
Administrative Unit Level 2 LangString 0..1 The region of the address, usually a province or state or similar area that typically includes multiple places.
bus number String 0..1 Officially assigned alphanumeric code added to the house number to distinguish multiple building units, pitches, moorings, or plots that share the same house number. Specialization in Address Presentation: location indication for Belgian addresses.
country LangString 0..1 Country where the address is located.
fullAddress LangString 0..1 The complete address in a single string, formatted or not. Avoids errors caused by splitting an address into its components. Displays the prescribed order of the different components.
house number String 0..1 Alphanumeric code officially assigned to building units, moorings, pitches, or plots. Specialization in Address Presentation: location indication for Belgian addresses.
location indication String 0..* Alphanumeric code that uniquely identifies the address locator within the street, administrative unit, etc.
location name LangString 0..* Name or description of the geographic object that the address locator indicates.
municipality name LangString 0..1 Municipality name of the address.
P.O. Box String 0..1 P.O. box number in a post office.
post name LangString 0..1 Name indicating the geographic area that groups addresses for postal purposes.
postal code String 0..1 Code indicating the geographic area that groups addresses for postal purposes.
refers to Belgian address 0..1 Address from which the address representation is derived. This is only possible for Belgian addresses, since an address is understood to be a Belgian address.
street name LangString 0..1 Street name of the address.

Contact info

Description
Information such as email, phone, address that allows contacting someone or something.
Usage
For example: a person or organization or service... Possible forms of contact: calling, emailing, etc.
Properties
The following properties are defined for this datatype: address , email , fax number , form of address , Name , telephone , website .
Property Expected Type Cardinality Description Usage Codelist
address Address representation 0..1 Address that can be written to or visited.
email String 0..1 Email address to which one can send emails.
fax number String 0..1 Fax number to which one can fax.
form of address LangString 0..1 Title with which someone is addressed or addressed or refers to someone. For example: Mr./Ms., Excellency, Doctor, ...
Name String 0..1 For example, the name of the person you can contact.
telephone String 0..1 Phone number to call.
website URI 0..1 Website you can surf to.

Location

Description
A location can be an identifiable geographic location (ISO 19112), but this location can also be a non-geographic location, such as a directory, row, or column. As such, there are countless ways location can be expressed.
Usage
To be used if the way the geographic position is indicated will only be established upon implementation. If this method is already known, then you must immediately work with Geometry, Geographic Name, Address, etc.
Properties
No properties are defined for this datatype.

Abstract class for temporal objects.

Temporal entities are temporal geometric primitives such as Moment or Period. This data type is abstract; use one of the subclasses.

Terminology used (external)

This section provides an overview of how terminology from vocabularies has been used in this model.

This implementation model relies on terms from these self-managed vocabularies:

  • https://data.vlaanderen.be/ns/persoon
  • https://implementatie.data.vlaanderen.be/ns/magda/persoon
  • https://data.vlaanderen.be/ns/generiek
  • https://implementatie.data.vlaanderen.be/ns/generiek
  • https://data.vlaanderen.be/ns/adres

External terminology, which falls outside the in-house namespace data.vlaanderen.be, is listed in the table below with the label, as found in the model, and the underlying URI.

When reusing external terminology, the principles of the SEMIC Style Guide are applied. This means that one agrees to the underlying definition, labels and restrictions associated with the URI in the context of the implementation model. The definitions, labels and usage notes must therefore not contradict those of the URI.
